summary.headline: Omnitech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore and PAT rose 468.7% to INR29.73 crore, with management guiding 35–40% YoY growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore, EBITDA rose 90.8% to INR50.62 crore, and PAT reached INR29.73 crore. Net working capital days fell to 233 from 294 at FY26-end, driven mainly by lower inventory and receivable days. Management reiterated an order book above INR3,000 crore and a two-facility capex programme of about INR250 crore at Chhapara. Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x from 0.34x, and cash fell to INR133.75 crore from INR163 crore.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: About 49% of Q1 revenue, down from about 52.7% in Q4 FY26. Pure oil and gas is below 40% of revenue per management.

segments.name: Others / diversified industrial applications
segments.commentary: About 6.9% of Q1 revenue, which management linked to early revenue from defence and aerospace first articles.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at about 35–40% YoY for FY28 (management said FY27/FY28 framing was on a YoY basis).
EBITDA margin guided at 30% and above.
Gross margin currently around 70%; management estimates a range of 68% to 71%.
Net working capital days target: a further 10–20% improvement, with historical levels below 200–220 days cited as the reference.
Two new facilities at Chhapara to be operationalised within about 14 months; the new Chhapara facility is expected to start commercial operations in FY28.
Depreciation moved from written-down value to straight-line method, expected to continue in coming quarters.
Defence and aerospace revenue expected over 1–3 years; some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28.
capex_capacity: Annualised machine-hour capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours across three plants: Metoda about 11 lakh, existing Chhapara about 19.5 lakh, Padavala about 1.37 lakh (as stated).
Capex of about INR250 crore for two new facilities at Chhapara: about INR100 crore buildings and INR150 crore plant and machinery, of which about INR25 crore is for existing Chhapara capacity.
Post-capex capacity is estimated at 42–43 lakh machine hours; capacity to be added in stages as machines are installed.
Some spillover of capex into FY28 is expected because of rain, with projects running about 1–1.5 months behind schedule.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad; no capex plan yet for these sites. Management said debt of INR390 crore remains after INR50 crore of IPO-funded repayment.
A 1.2 MW solar plant funded from IPO capex has started generating power.
demand_pricing: Order book is above INR3,000 crore as of 31 July 2026, including a multi-year Weatherford order exceeding USD100 million. About INR2,000 crore relates to two large orders with 3–5 year execution, and about INR1,000 crore is short- to moderate-cycle (6–18 months).

Geographic mix in Q1: North America 52%, Asia 27%, India 17%, Europe/UK 3%; exports about 78% of revenue. Management expects North America at 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe growing.

Management said raw-material cost changes are passed to customers through pass-through mechanisms and quarterly business reviews, with a lag of about 2–3 months; it also cited forex pass-through. It said 100% pass-through.
Existing facilities can generate about INR800–900 crore of annual revenue, per management.
Asset turnover of about 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% expected over time, per management.
Nadcap accreditation is in progress and defence/aerospace first articles are underway; approvals may take 6–15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are machine-hour capacities by site, and what is the capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours; the INR250 crore capex (INR100 crore building, INR150 crore plant) takes this to 42–43 lakh hours, with about INR25 crore of the machinery for existing Chhapara.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and timing of the large-order execution from the two anchor orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution has started, with an expected run-rate of about INR50 crore and more, ramping over years one to five; short-cycle industrial orders of about 3–4 months are also being executed.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be assessed for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 35–40% growth and EBITDA margin of 30% and above, and said margins are capability-driven with product-level variation of 1–2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost rise sequentially and what is the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed changes to product mix in a low-volume, high-mix business and to a 2–3 month lag tied to quarterly reviews; it said pass-through is 100%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scalable revenue potential from the new capex and what ROCE should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants can do about INR800–900 crore a year. New capacity will be added in stages; management expects asset turnover of 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% at peak, though this takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further working capital improvement, and what is the order-book geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a further 10–20% improvement, citing minimum MOQ needs for new vertical first articles. North America is 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe making up 10–20%.

risks_watch: Capex spillover into FY28 and about 1–1.5 months of schedule delay due to rain.
Working capital remains elevated at 233 days, and management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high.
Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x and cash fell by about INR29 crore quarter-end to quarter-end (from INR163 crore to INR133.75 crore).
Sequential raw-material cost increase (transcript cites 20%, 24%, then 28%) and the 2–3 month pass-through lag.
Defence and aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) are not complete and timing is uncertain.
Revenue concentration: energy is 49% of revenue and 78% of revenue is exports; North America is 52%.

key_quotes: So, we are having a very strong order book as of now, and we are skeptical to taking the more bigger orders also.
But we are right on track as far as the FA approvals are concerned and also the process which are in line for us to get approved.
So, it is not a segment-specific, but of course, sometimes in a some product we may have a some 2%, 3%, 4% lesser margin, and some product have a little bit more margin.
So, it takes around 2 to 3 months to pass through that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, order book and capacity, with a bullish 35–40% YoY outlook and 30%+ EBITDA margin framing. Cautious and evasive on specifics: margins are described as capability-driven with no segment detail, FA/defence timing is hedged on approvals, and the net debt ratio and raw-material pass-through lag were addressed only loosely.

New Chhapara facility commercial operations expected in FY28

growth.why: Management guides 35-40% YoY revenue growth (midpoint 37.5%) for FY28, backed by an order book above INR3,000 cr and INR250 cr of Chhapara capacity expansion taking machine-hour capacity from ~31-32 lakh to 42-43 lakh hours, though part of the capex may spill into FY28 due to rain delays.
